meta.title: Inspection Lab - Reading a Failed Hook

modules.intro: One 1v1 pull, run exactly the way the tournament will run in September.
modules.title: The Match
modules.aiNote: No AI. You were in the room and it happened once.

blocks.content:
Two hooks, linked in one load path, pulled against each other until one breaks.

**Call it before the pull.** Which hook survives, and where will the loser go. Write it down first. Being wrong is worth more than being right, because the gap between what you called and what happened is the only thing on this page that changes how you design.

Then fill both rows: the one that broke and the one that did not.

columns.label: What you called before the pull

columns.tip: Look closely at the survivor. Cracks, whitening, bending.
columns.label: Condition after

blocks.prompt: The winning hook advances to the next match in whatever condition it is now in. Based on what you can see on it, would you send it again, or hold it back and send your other hook?

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Both rows filled, each carrying a call made before the pull and what actually happened beside it.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Only one hook recorded, or the call column was filled in once the result was already known.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Table empty, or written from memory after the demonstration ended.

rubric.criterion: A call was made before the pull and both hooks are recorded

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Names something specific observed on the surviving hook and reasons from it to a decision.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Reaches a decision but supports it with general reasoning rather than with what is on the part.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Blank, or an answer that would read identically for any hook in any condition.

rubric.criterion: The send-or-hold judgment reasons from the survivor's actual condition

modules.intro: Take a hook out of the box of past-tournament breaks and run the full inspection on it.
modules.title: The Lab
modules.aiNote: No AI. You are reading instruments. There is nothing here to look up.

blocks.content:
Take one hook from the box, a set of calipers or a ruler, and the scale.

**Record what the calipers say, not whether it passed.** A hook that reads 61.4 g failed by 1.4 g, and a hook that reads 88 g was never close. Those are different parts and "fail" hides the difference. Numbers first, verdict second.

Work one row at a time. If a check does not apply to your hook because that part of it is gone, write what is missing.

columns.tip: Mass, thickness, anchor diameter, throat at its narrowest, centre to centre.
columns.label: Check

columns.tip: A number with units. Every one of these is measurable.
columns.label: What the instrument reads

columns.tip: Compare your number against the rules guide.
columns.label: Legal?

blocks.prompt: Which check would have been hardest for this hook to pass when it was new, and how do your own numbers tell you that?

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: All five checks carry a reading with units, and a legality call beside each one.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Four checks carry readings with units; one is missing a value or its units.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Most rows record only legal or illegal, or units are missing throughout.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Table empty, or filled from the rules guide rather than from an instrument.

rubric.criterion: Measurements are recorded as instrument readings, not as verdicts

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Names a specific check and points at a reading from the table above as the reason.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Names a check but gives a general reason rather than a number from the table.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Blank, or names something that is not one of the inspection checks.

rubric.criterion: The hardest-check judgment is supported by the student's own readings

modules.intro: From the case library. Two designs, and what each one gives you.
modules.title: Two Designs You Are Borrowing From
modules.aiNote: COACH only. Ask it to explain how a design works or what a feature does. Do not ask it which designs to pick or what your hook should look like.

blocks.content:
Find two designs in the case library that your concept takes something from.

**Name what you are taking, not what the design is.** "It has a thick throat" describes it. "I am taking its throat fillet because the throat is where three of today's hooks broke" is what this is asking for.

Two different designs. Not two views of one.

columns.tip: Slide number or name from the library.
columns.label: Design

columns.tip: Tie it to something you saw or measured today.
columns.label: Why that helps your hook

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Two distinct designs named, each with a specific feature and a reason tied to the match or to a measurement taken today.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Two designs named but described in general terms, or only one reason connects to today's evidence.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: One design or none, or the same design listed twice.

rubric.criterion: Each borrowed idea is specific and tied to evidence from today

modules.intro: On paper. Photograph it and upload it here.
modules.title: Concept Sketch
modules.aiNote: No AI. Drawn by your hand, dimensioned by your hand.

blocks.content:
Sketch your hook by hand and put **five dimensions** on it: overall length, both hole diameters, centre to centre, throat opening width, and thickness.

Numbers, not proportions. "About this wide" is not a dimension.

This sketch is what you build from tomorrow. A student who opens SolidWorks without numbers spends the period nudging geometry until it looks right and ends up with a part nobody can check against the rules.

items: Centre to centre is dimensioned and falls between 2.000 and 2.500
Throat opening width is dimensioned and is at least 0.750
Thickness is dimensioned and is 1.00 or under
My teammate's name is written on the sketch, and we have agreed whether our two hooks are the same design or different

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: All five dimensions present and readable, and every one falls inside the rules.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: All five dimensions present, but at least one value breaks a rule in the guide.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Sketch uploaded with three or four dimensions on it, or values given as ranges rather than numbers.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Nothing uploaded, or a drawing with fewer than three dimensions on it.

rubric.criterion: The sketch is dimensioned well enough to build from
